ai.description: This frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct, prominent tubercle on the humerus and lacks a vocal sac. It is distinguished by a granular dorsum and a pale, dark-edged interorbital bar.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes tuberohumerus* is best distinguished by the prominent, distinct tubercle located on the upper arm (humerus), a feature absent in most similar bush frogs.
ai.habitat: The Kudremukh bush frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kudremukh bush frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small insects among the foliage of the Western Ghats' high-altitude forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes tuberohumerus* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes tuberohumerus* is endemic to the central Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Kudremukh Bush Frog emits a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests and grasslands.
